title: Occlusion realism in optical see-through AR
bottleneck: Virtual objects should be hidden behind real ones, but optical see-through displays can't block real light: they add light but can't subtract it, so virtual objects look ghostly and never properly occlude. Pixel-level occlusion needs per-pixel light modulators that don't exist in glasses form factors. Video see-through solves it with cameras but adds latency and isolates the user.
why_it_blocks: Without correct occlusion, AR objects float unconvincingly over reality, breaking the core illusion. The additive-only nature of waveguides is a physics wall for optical AR realism.
current_state: Dimming layers (electrochromic) provide coarse occlusion; video see-through headsets achieve good occlusion at the cost of camera latency. True per-pixel occlusion in optical AR is unsolved. Coarse dimming layers can darken regions of the view but cannot carve the pixel-precise silhouettes that real occlusion needs.
